  "text": "# CLAUDE.md

Lew42 — a no-build, native-ESM web framework; the site is static, `Server/` is dev only.
This file rules; skills and readmes elaborate it. **Do not edit it without asking.**

This file holds the laws, safety and cost rules every agent needs. The framework's own rules (presentation, readmes and docs, classes, pages, the live site, traps) live in `public/framework/readme.md` and the doc it links, `public/framework/doc/rules.md`; the long form of the safety and cost rules is `public/framework/ai/doc/agent-rules.md`. Split 2026-10-22: every old sentence is mapped to its new home in `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/sessions-and-tasks/readme-roles/moves.md`; reworded ones keep their old wording in `public/framework/ai/doc/claude-md-archive.md`.

## Read first, in this order

1. **`public/framework/readme.md`** — mandatory for every agent: the module index and the framework's rules. Before you write a page, a readme, a class or anything the owner reads, also read the rule it links (`public/framework/doc/rules.md`).
2. **Your role's readme** — `Servex/agents/roles/readme.md` lists them (minion, mastermind, reviewer, clarity). A Servex agent gets its own readme in its first message; a VS Code tab reads it by hand.
3. **`public/framework/ai/handover.md`** and `git log --oneline -20` (below, "Where to look").

Any agent, Claude or not, starts from the short base in `public/framework/ai/agents.md`.

## Laws

1. **Less is more — ASAP, As Simple As Possible.** Fastest working version first, then improve. Show, don't tell — a demo you can open beats a description. Question every word, line, section. Deep docs may breathe.
2. **Clear beats brief — by far.** Simple, but clear: explain it like I'm five. Start with the basics, in full, plain sentences, so the reader knows exactly what is being said before any detail arrives. Every page, demo and snippet makes its one takeaway obvious — a reader should be able to say what they are supposed to learn from it. Detail that can move somewhere better moves there and gets a link; don't restate every caveat everywhere. An extra sentence that clarifies a necessary point belongs. "Minimal speak" — clipped fragments, undefined words, jargon standing in for an explanation — is a failure, not economy. New coders are the audience. (the owner, 2026-09-04)
3. **Prioritize.** Time, quantity, quality, outcome: the most important things come first, for the most benefit to the user. Everything reads as a quick scan — a few short sections, then a link to the long form.
4. **Follow the owner's words.** Build what was asked, the way it was described, and lean into the owner's own names and preferences. Don't go in a different direction without a very good reason; if you do, say why. (the owner, 2026-09-30)
5. **Keep working; never wait on the owner.** Make the best decision, say what the alternative was, and keep going. Never create a request that blocks on the owner: they may never see it. If a limit stops you, queue the work and pick it up after. Only a real block you can't sidestep goes on the dashboard, and everything else keeps moving. Don't do anything dangerous. (the owner, 2026-09-30) **A real block (killing a process, deleting data, spending money) is filed as a task waiting on the owner (`{"wait":{"on":"owner"}}`, so `list_waiting` shows it), and the agent that filed it asks again at every check-in until it is answered. A question left in a report is a dropped task. Then fix the root cause, so the next case needs no approval.** (the owner, 2026-11-06: a process kill list from 11-04 waited for a yes nobody asked for again.) The owner often dictates long-winded rants, ideas, tasks or lectures while looking away and may never read your reply: **assume ephemeral chat logs will never be read again.** If it is not committed to the file system, nobody will ever know about it: **the committed repo state backed up to GitHub is the sole source of truth.** Never leave loose ends hanging on the assumption of a follow-up. If there is a safe, quick fix, attempt it; if not, **record the essence of the dictation immediately in the proper place** (notes, legitimate questions, tradeoffs or implications): a short `doc/*.md` file beside the relevant module, linked from that directory's `readme.md`. Files are what survive. (the owner, 2026-10-01, updated 2026-10-05)
6. **One of everything; don't repeat yourself.** Before you build, find what already exists and use it, or extend it. Never build a second version of a system. Every surface that shows the same thing (a chat, a sidebar, a card, a rail) uses the same component, so one fix updates all of them. (the owner, 2026-09-30)
7. **Compute, don't recall.** Anything a computer can work out (state, counts, costs, which tasks landed, log lines, records) is done by a node script or tool that reads the real state, never written by an AI from memory. AI handles judgment; record-keeping is code. (the owner, 2026-10-01)
8. **Name it and home it first.** Every new module or task settles its name and home location first. (the owner, 2026-10-16)
9. **Document the structure as you build.** Every system's readme states what it is, its exact on-disk structure, which tool writes its data and from where, and which class reads it — verified against the code, no history. If an agent had to investigate to learn how a system works, the readme failed; fix the readme in the same task. (the owner, 2026-10-19)
10. **Index everything you create.** Every file, folder, task, child session or page you make is recorded in its parent the moment it exists: a task folder in its session record, a child session under its parent, a page in its parent's `children:` or a link, a system in its readme. Anything unindexed is forgotten. (the owner, 2026-10-23)

## Memory, history, safety (long form: `public/framework/ai/doc/agent-rules.md`)

- **Context must not die in sessions:** decisions and insight go to the page or module they concern, linked to the source prompt, never left in chat. Post an update or log line at least every ~5 minutes of work.
- **File each ask the first time:** as a task on the session's record or a one-line note in the readme it concerns (`core/Task/readme.md`, "Using tasks").
- **Link, don't regenerate:** reference the prompt, session, task or doc by link; never retype what is written.
- **Never destructive:** don't delete logs, merge records or overwrite history; if something must go, move it aside and say so. Git is the undo.
- **Moves and renames are scripted, never retyped:** a node script with a dry run and a manifest of every old to new path. Then link anything that exists in the repo but not on the site.
- **Commit after every working step:** smoke-test, then commit, in a worktree; merge after reviewing the diff; keep GitHub current: `merge.mjs` pushes michael/dev after each landing, and a commit made straight on michael/dev is pushed too. (the owner, 2026-10-29)
- **Stream, don't poll:** anything real-time is a JSONL append and a `live()` tail, never `setInterval` + `fetch`.

## Cost and roles (long form: `public/framework/ai/doc/agent-rules.md`)

- **Usage pace:** a mastermind runs `node Server/usage-now.mjs` when it starts and before each spawn. Over pace: Sonnet by default, no Opus without a stated reason, fewer agents.
- **Audits go to Haiku, under 100k tokens:** aim for 30–60k per request; a node script chunks big inputs. Sonnet is for UI and object-oriented code.
- **Mind the token burn:** let a script read and calculate, batch tool calls, no session replays or long audits unless asked, keep sessions short.
- **No hard fences between roles:** a capable agent just does the job; the mastermind is the one that decides and splits work.

## Ask before

- Breaking a constraint: no build step (`public/` runs as-is; imports are real `.js` URLs), no server at runtime (production is static), no new npm dependency (`npx` and global tools are fine).
- Major surgery: renaming a core API, moving a responsibility, anything with a dozen callers.

## Where to look

- **First, every new session:** `public/framework/ai/handover.md` (state of the world, what is open) and `git log --oneline -20` (what landed recently). Query the logs only when you need a detail; never read them whole. (the owner, 2026-10-09)
- **Past work, any question about what was asked or done:** `public/framework/ai/indexing-past-work.md`: one `git grep` over the session logs (rg is not installed), the owner's own words per channel, the raw transcripts, git history, and a map of every index we already have. A search that misses or needs a second try gets its working query added there.
- `readme.md` (root) — setup, branches, deploy
- `public/framework/readme.md` — THE module index (every module, one line, one link) and the framework's rules; every agent reads it ("Read first", above).
- `public/framework/ai/` — the task log: open a task before the first edit (`new-task`), log as you go, land it (`finish-task`)
- `Server/` — dev server only
- `Servex/` — the agent system: roles, sessions, spawning, the quick-fix pool, the heartbeat, merge and review. Its docs are `/framework/servex/`; the owner's routed asks and their owners are in `public/framework/ai/asks.jsonl`
- `public/framework/ai/doc/audits.md` — every audit of what the owner asked against what was done; for new loose ends, the prompt audit (`node Server/PromptAudit.mjs --days 7`, doc `ai/doc/prompt-audit.md`). Check it before building another audit.
- Scratch — scripts, transcripts, intermediate JSON — goes in the session scratchpad, not the repo
"

11. **Readmes are the index.** Each lists everything directly inside its folder (or links a sub-doc that does), and points to closely related modules elsewhere. When a lookup is hard, write the search recipe into the nearest readme once you've solved it. Finding past work: [indexing-past-work.md](indexing-past-work.md). Long form: [doc/rules.md](../doc/rules.md), "Readmes are the cheap index". (the owner, 2026-11-06)
12. **Every class gets one lean core test** (`X.test.mjs` beside it): make one instance, exercise the top ~50% of what it does, assert after each call, and stay well under 1 s. Add it when you build or first change a class that has none; don't over-test. How, and what earns more: [core/Test](../core/Test/readme.md).

## ⚠ One folder per session (the owner, asked many times; 2026-11-06)

A session has exactly ONE folder: `public/framework/ai/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<folder>/`, the day it began. The url `/framework/ai/sessions/<uuid>/` only redirects there; never create, name or write a folder `sessions/<uuid>/`. Your session's folder is printed at start ("Your session is …; its one folder is …"). In code, find it with `SessionFolders.at(store).of(id)` (its own folder) or `.record_of(id)` (where its record sits, nested for a spawned agent) ([core/Session/SessionFolders.mjs](../core/Session/SessionFolders.mjs)), never by building a path. Make it with `.create(id, {first})` (or `Session.create({id, name, parent, first})`), the one creator. A check fails loudly on a flat folder: `node Server/SessionConsolidate.mjs --check`. Details: [sessions/doc/one-folder.md](sessions/doc/one-folder.md).

## Memory, history, safety (long form: [doc/agent-rules.md](doc/agent-rules.md))

- **Context must not die in sessions:** decisions and insight go to the page or module they concern, linked to the source prompt, never left in chat. Post an update or log line at least every ~5 minutes of work.
- **File each ask the first time:** as a task on the session's record or a one-line note in the readme it concerns (`core/Task/readme.md`, "Using tasks").
- **Work as a task:** open a task before real work, log as you go, close it with an outcome and evidence ([doc/task-buckets.md](doc/task-buckets.md)). A fresh agent must be able to continue from the task folder alone.
- **Link, don't regenerate:** reference the prompt, session, task or doc by link; never retype what is written.
- **Never destructive:** don't delete logs, merge records or overwrite history; if something must go, move it aside and say so. Git is the undo. Never push with force or skip hooks.
- **Moves and renames are scripted, never retyped:** a node script with a dry run and a manifest of every old to new path. Then link anything that exists in the repo but not on the site.
- **Commit after every working step:** smoke-test, then commit by exact path, in a worktree; merge after reviewing the diff; keep GitHub current: `merge.mjs` pushes michael/dev after each landing, and a commit made straight on michael/dev is pushed too. (the owner, 2026-10-29)
- **Stream, don't poll:** anything real-time is a JSONL append and a `live()` tail, never `setInterval` + `fetch`.

## Cost and roles (long form: [doc/agent-rules.md](doc/agent-rules.md))

- **Usage pace:** a mastermind runs `node Server/usage-now.mjs` when it starts and before each spawn. Over pace: Sonnet by default, no Opus without a stated reason, fewer agents.
- **Audits go to Haiku, under 100k tokens:** aim for 30–60k per request; a node script chunks big inputs. Sonnet is for UI and object-oriented code.
- **Mind the token burn:** let a script read and calculate, batch tool calls, no session replays or long audits unless asked, keep sessions short.
- **Context size:** keep a working agent rather than switching for context size alone; compact around 300k. Decisions go in the module's docs as they are made ([doc/context.md](doc/context.md)).
- **No hard fences between roles:** a capable agent just does the job; the mastermind is the one that decides and splits work.

## Explaining to the owner

- **Show an API as JavaScript or pseudocode** (`page.tabs.add({name: "today"})`), not as a JSON delta, unless the owner asks what the delta looks like. Say which object the call operates on (`page`, `page.items`, a card). (the owner, 2026-11-06)

## Ask before

- Breaking a constraint: no build step (`public/` runs as-is; imports are real `.js` URLs), no server at runtime (production is static), no new npm dependency (`npx` and global tools are fine).
- Major surgery: renaming a core API, moving a responsibility, anything with a dozen callers.

## Where to look

- **First, every new session:** [handover.md](handover.md) (the state of the world, what is open) and `git log --oneline -20` (what landed recently). Query the logs only when you need a detail; never read them whole. (the owner, 2026-10-09)
- **Past work, any question about what was asked or done:** [indexing-past-work.md](indexing-past-work.md): one `git grep` over the session logs (rg is not installed), the owner's own words per channel, the raw transcripts, git history, and a map of every index we already have. A search that misses or needs a second try gets its working query added there.
- `readme.md` (root): setup, branches, deploy.
- [public/framework/readme.md](../readme.md): THE module index (every module, one line, one link) and the framework's rules.
- `public/framework/ai/`: the task log. Open a task before the first edit (`new-task`), log as you go, land it (`finish-task`).
- `Server/`: dev server only.
- `Servex/`: the agent system (roles, sessions, spawning, the quick-fix pool, the heartbeat, merge and review). Its docs are `/framework/servex/`; the owner's routed asks and their owners are in [asks.jsonl](asks.jsonl).
- [doc/audits.md](doc/audits.md): every audit of what the owner asked against what was done; for new loose ends, the prompt audit (`node Server/PromptAudit.mjs --days 7`, doc [doc/prompt-audit.md](doc/prompt-audit.md)). Check it before building another audit.
- Scratch (scripts, transcripts, intermediate JSON) goes in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Probable direction: agents in the dev server (the owner, 2026-11-06; not built)

SDK agents would run inside each project's dev server, not in Servex. That gives one item cache shared by the browser, the agents and MCP. Servex would shrink to a manager, and each project would get its own scoped MCP and `spawn_agent`. Tradeoffs, open questions and the alternative: [Servex/readme.md](../../../Servex/readme.md#probable-direction-agents-run-in-the-projects-dev-server-the-owner-2026-11-06-not-built). Until it is built, nothing changes: agents still run in Servex.

## Where this file goes

How it reaches an agent, and why it is a system prompt and not a message: [doc/agent-base-proposal.md](doc/agent-base-proposal.md). Claude Code reaches it through `CLAUDE.md`, which imports it.

content.text:
Your core point: **asks get lost between your words and finished work.** Everything else is a symptom of that. Here's the plan.

## Done just now
- **`CLAUDE.md` is now one line,** an import of `ai/agents.md`. All twelve laws and the rules sections moved into agents.md with nothing dropped, and I checked that every link in it resolves. There's a new rule too: nothing gets added to CLAUDE.md again.
- **Found by search, which proves the indexing works:** the map of all audits (`ai/doc/audits.md`), the prompt refinement map (`ai/doc/prompt-refinement-map.md`, which lists **8** mechanisms, not 14), and **94 session files** from Oct–Nov that say something like "waiting on you" or "your call".

## Top priority: fix the pipe that loses asks
```text
your words → sentences → placed in tasks
  → task handed off whole → closed with proof
```
1. **Capture:** keep your raw sentences on every channel. *(session-truth, in progress)*
2. **Place:** every sentence gets placed into a task. A sentence that isn't placed anywhere is a red flag. Keep **one** of the 8 refinement mechanisms and retire the rest, after taking their lessons.
3. **Hand off the task itself,** with your sentences attached, never a paraphrase. That ends the telephone game. `spawn_agent` can already move a task into a child (`task: {from, id}`); it needs to become the default.
4. **Close with proof.** Anything left under 100% becomes a task waiting on you, and **/live/truth/** shows the numbers daily. *(session-truth)*
5. **Every process logged** with a start and an exit. *(resources, already live)*

## Second priority
6. **Mentions index:** a prompt mentioning `@Page` gets tagged automatically, and each module lists the prompts that mention it. That's code only, so it's cheap.
7. **Readmes as system maps:** each readme names its related modules and lists its search terms, as regex. Start with Item/List/Page, sessions, Servex, and the Dictate/Refine/Recite family.
8. **A calibrated past-work audit:** a cheap model, newest first, one prompt at a time, matching sentence → task → commit. Start with the 94 "waiting on you" moments, and calibrate on 3–5 sessions you judge yourself before scaling up.
9. **Lessons from old systems,** written down before they're retired.
10. **Later:** a small node filter for multi-field JSONL queries, compressed archives of the raw transcripts, and a database only if `git grep` stops being fast enough.

## Decisions I made
- **One doc, not two.** Indexing and search stay together in `indexing-past-work.md`, since they go hand in hand. If it grows, the search recipes split out into `searching.md`.
- **Steps 2–3 start after session-truth lands capture.** They build on it, and running both at once would collide. Usage is at 65% of pace, so there's room for one more mastermind after that.

# Past-work audits: the design (not running yet)

The owner's design, 2026-11-06. Nothing here runs until it has been calibrated, and then only when there is usage to spare. Every earlier audit is listed in [audits.md](audits.md); read it first, and learn from what didn't work.

## The goal

Fix the **system** that lets asks get lost, not just chase each loose end. An audit is worth running only if it changes the system: the logging, the instructions, the task flow.

## Two kinds

1. **Prompt audit.** The owner's own words, **newest first**, one prompt at a time. Skip agent-to-agent messages: a task handed down is the same task, not a new one, so there's no double accounting.
2. **System audit.** Per system group, then per directory, then per file. Is it used? Is it stable? Is it documented and mapped to its neighbours? Keep it, merge it, or retire it (write the lessons down first, then move it aside; never delete). The groups:
   - Item, List and Page
   - sessions and tasks
   - Servex, AI, roles, SDK and MCP
   - the web voice chat (Dictate, Recite, Refine)

   Folders that follow one known structure (session folders, `tasks/`) are checked as a pattern, not file by file. Readmes get a per-readme pass: is each statement still true, still needed, and linked?

## One instruction set, live and after the fact

Prompt refinement is the same step whether it runs live (the web voice chat, placing each sentence as it arrives) or after the fact (this audit). When it improves, rerun it on past prompts and compare the results. Its 8 current mechanisms are listed in [prompt-refinement-map.md](prompt-refinement-map.md); keep one.

## What each prompt yields (fixed before the first real run)

Settle this list once, so a forgotten field never forces a costly rerun:

- the asks, primary and secondary, in the owner's words
- the questions the owner asked
- mentions and tags (`@Page`, paths, modules)
- priority signals: anger, "I've asked this before"
- red flags: "waiting on you", "your call", "needs your yes", each one followed up to see if it was ever answered
- the status of each ask **judged against the current state**: done, still valid, or no longer relevant (not "was it done at the time")

## Context

- **One prompt in isolation:** cheap, but it loses context and gets things wrong. That's the weakness of the old HITL "clarity" pipeline, which sent each chunk to a fresh session.
- **The whole session replayed up to that prompt:** full context, but it can cost hundreds of dollars with a big model, and may be cheap with Haiku.

Calibration decides which to use.

## Calibration before anything runs

1. Take 3–5 recent prompts.
2. Run Haiku, then Sonnet, then Opus on the same prompts with the same instructions.
3. Compare the results; the owner judges them.
4. Freeze the instructions and the output fields, then scale up with the cheapest model that matches.

## Budget gate

- Run audits only while the weekly pace is **under 50%** (`node Server/usage-now.mjs`).
- Never start a batch at the week's reset, because it would burn the new week at once.
- Go slowly: one prompt at a time, in the background.

## Sources

| Source | Where |
|---|---|
| VS Code prompts | `Prompt` lines in session logs (the `UserPromptSubmit` hook) |
| Web voice chat | `sentences` in session logs |
| Claude app sessions (voice and text) | the cloud workspace's own transcript (`~/.claude/projects/-home-claude/<id>.jsonl` *in the cloud*); it has to be brought to the PC first |
| Everything else | raw transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/C--Code-lew42-monorepo/` |

How to search them: [../indexing-past-work.md](../indexing-past-work.md).

## Related ideas from the same prompt (written down, not built)

- **Plan extends Task.** It's probably a `core/Task/Process.js` subclass. A plan waits for approval before it runs. Quick tasks just run; long or hard ones get a plan first.
- **Requirements vs steps.** Subtasks that can be done in any order are requirements; ordered ones are a Process's steps.
- **Partial completion.** A task can be 0.5 or 0.8 done, and its parents average it in. Proof can be hallucinated, so "closed with proof" is a check, not a guarantee.
- **Mentions as tags.** A mention in a prompt or on a page tags it, and the mentioned thing keeps a backlink list (e.g. `mentions.jsonl`).
- **Readme reads.** Track whether agents actually read the readmes they should. The first step of any task is reading the right readmes. A script flags readmes that grow too long, rather than enforcing a hard limit.

~/.claude/projects/-home-claude/

- **Two kinds of audit:** your own prompts, newest first, skipping agent chatter; and systems, one group at a time, then down to directories and files.

- **Fixed output fields,** settled before the first real run.
- **Judged against the current state,** not against what was true at the time.
- **"Waiting on you" moments get red-flagged.**

- **Only while the weekly pace is under 50%.** It's about 65% now, so nothing runs yet.
- **Ideas in the same doc:** Plan extends Process and waits for approval; requirements vs steps; partial completion; mentions as tags; tracking which readmes actually get read.
